correctness.rationale: The claim is a finite, well-defined exact joint-population census of \(3^{14}\) labelled Heawood colorings. One classifier enumerates every ternary state and applies indegree peeling; a separately written classifier uses binary-dot-product Fano incidence and active-path recursion. Each finite-functional-graph algorithm computes true least eventual period by a proved invariant; both return the ten identical classes summing to 4,782,969, and replay from embedded files succeeds. Third-presentation trajectory checks validate both discrepancy types and the independent GHM marginal matches published exact counts. The proof is exhaustive finite enumeration, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The Heawood Fano incidence network is the smallest cubic graph with girth six and a natural benchmark for graph excitation. The complete joint period distribution is an intrinsic finite dynamical invariant of two canonical rules from exactly the same initial states, not a narrow arbitrary slice or a repeat of the GHM marginal. The new ten-to-five channel alongside the eight-to-four channel separates two qualitatively distinct cross-model resonances; exact basin sizes and exclusion of all other discrepancies motivate precise future network comparisons.
